applicable_when: The kernel is a pure strided-scatter copy: it reads a flat (1960,64) tensor and writes into a non-contiguous (10,64,14,14) output with stride-512 stores. With XBLOCK=128 fixed, the grid has only 980 CTAs across 132 SMs (~0.46 waves). Each CTA issues only 4 loads and 4 stores (128 elements / 32 threads = 4 per thread), giving too few in-flight memory requests to hide L1TEX latency (53% of stall cycles). Increasing XBLOCK to 512 or 1024 reduces the grid to 245-123 CTAs but each CTA issues 16-32 memory ops per thread, dramatically increasing memory-level parallelism per warp. Pairing with num_warps=8 doubles the warp pool per block, giving the scheduler more eligible warps to hide latency. @triton.autotune lets the runtime pick the best config without manual tuning.
